g.title: The promise 'this will keep resolving' — breaking it is a breach, not an event.
One narrowing supplied by a reference-act — connected to its referent by an agreement or by a fact, and nothing else.
The location a path routes to.
A thing whose identity is independent of its current description — it persists through change.
How many the actor believes exist — 'no more than three, or I've grossly misunderstood the data.'
How many referents the actor means to pick out — part of the act's type, knowable before resolution, and what gives a miss its meaning.
Whoever maintains a designator's binding — a family, a filesystem, a store.
How many the act will touch — 'change the first,' 'take them all.'
The location a path routes from.
Descriptors past the minimum needed to reach one referent — they are verification and redundant routes, never waste.
One set of monotonic steps between two locations.
What an engine resolves relative to: an origin, a scope, a moment, a policy about what counts as the world.
The promise 'this resolves today, and it's the one we'd rather you use.'
Per-hop ownership of resolution: each intermediate location routes only its next hop.
'The address you gave us is ambiguous and there are several people by that name it might end up with.' — the refused package that opens the postal model
The thing a reference-act intends to pick out.
What performs resolution — never a property of the act itself.
Why order appears in an address at all — and exactly what an engine may optimize.
The promise 'this names IT' — held by the minting community, independent of routability.
A thing that IS its description — 'which one' is a meaningless question.
A predicate the world satisfies — nothing was ever bound; the connection is recomputed from whatever satisfies it at each use.
A minted name bound to its referent by convention — the binding, not the referent's properties, is the whole connection.
A path routable to its destination from any origin (within a bounded context).
No promise at all: whatever route works from here, now — expected to expire with its context.
A containment claim over a designated container — 'contained in c', where c is named by a containment-coordinate.
The name of one nesting container inside a location chain.
A designator for the target itself, as opposed to its containers.
A non-terminal step of a path that is itself a location.
